summary: Both sides are alive, mirror-symmetric and beat120-reactive with identical (gauge-only) control surfaces, but the port draws a sparse single-pixel speckle field that strobes to near-black on every 2 Hz beat in 2-3 hues, where the original draws a dense, persistent, full-rainbow field of contiguous smooth blobs that never darkens — ~6x dimmer, ~3x fewer lit pixels, ~3x less hue diversity, and spatially uncorrelated with the original's field.
observations: Rig/defaults: 16x16 grid, 256 px. Both sides report wantsSensors: true and were fed sensorModel beat120 (sensors: "synth") on every run; no compile or runtime errors on either side.

Control surface MATCHES exactly: both sides expose the same three display-only controls — gaugeFeedback ("Feedback"), gaugeGain ("Gain"), gaugeComplexity ("Complexity"), all kind=gauge. --probe-controls reports "(no settable controls)" for both, so there are no dials to sweep and no control-surface finding.

BRIGHTNESS GAP ~6x, stable over 240 s. survey240 (240 s @ 10 fps) meanBrightness avg: orig 84.9 (trend steady, min 6 max 255), port 15.0 (trend volatile, min 1 max 135). Per-10 s bucket means are flat on both after warm-up: orig 76-100 throughout t=10..240 s, port 11-17 throughout. baseline (6 s @ 20 fps): orig 153, port 50. late (--skip 200, 20 s @ 20 fps): orig 129, port 30.

DENSITY GAP ~3x. Lit-pixel fraction from --dump (max channel > 0): original 80-100% of the grid at every sampled steady-state time (t=2.25..32.95 s); port 22-41%. Same at 48x48 (grid48d): orig 80-97% lit, port 24-30% lit.

RHYTHM: the port hard-strobes at exactly 2 Hz, the original does not. dense20 (--skip 30, 3 s @ 20 fps, 60 consecutive dumped frames): port's whole-grid mean max-channel is a clean sawtooth — attack to ~65-71 on each beat at t=30.05/30.55/31.05/31.55/32.05/32.55 s, then exponential decay to ~5-7 just before the next beat (i.e. it is essentially black between beats). Original over the same 60 frames sits at 141-225 and drifts slowly downward with no beat-scale dip at all.

Confirmed numerically by autocorrelation of the survey motion series (10 fps, 600 frames): port peaks at lag 5 (r=0.72) with strong harmonics at 10/15/20/25/30/35/40 — locked to the 0.5 s beat. Original's motion peaks at lag 1 (r=0.51) with lag 5 only r=0.47 — it has a beat component but is dominated by smooth frame-to-frame continuity. Original meanBrightness autocorr is 0.96 at lag 1 and still 0.61 at lag 8; the port's falls to 0.48 by lag 7.

PER-PIXEL FADE: original decays x0.80 per frame at 20 fps (measured chain 255->220->176->141->112->90->72->57, half-life 3.1 frames = 0.155 s); port decays x0.60 per frame (217->135->83->50->30 and 244->146->87->52->31->18->11->6->4->2->1->0, half-life 1.36 frames = 0.068 s). So the port's fade is ~2.3x too fast in the tail — but the bigger effect is re-trigger rate: original pixels sit railed at 255 for 10-20 consecutive frames before any decay begins, port pixels fire once per beat for ~4-6 frames then run all the way to 0 and stay there.

COLOR: original steady state occupies 10-12 of 12 hue bins SIMULTANEOUSLY in every frame (a full spatial rainbow), plus ~50/256 pure-white pixels. Port occupies only 1-5 bins per frame. At t=31.05 s the port's entire lit set is three hues — ~0/36 (red), ~15-17/36 (cyan), ~33-36/36 (magenta-red) — with no greens, yellows or blues anywhere; the original at the same instant spans the whole wheel with hues varying smoothly across space.

SPATIAL TEXTURE is the biggest structural divergence. Nearest-neighbour autocorrelation of the max-channel field in steady state (t=30..32.4 s): original 0.44-0.86 (smooth, contiguous blobs and contour bands), port 0.17-0.29 (uncorrelated salt-and-pepper single-pixel speckle). Visible directly at --grid 48x48: the original draws thick continuous rainbow contour bands (nested arches, rings, mirrored 'tree' shapes) filling the whole canvas; the port draws thin, broken, mostly-white speckled lines on black.

The two value fields are genuinely unrelated, not one field with a different output mapping. At 48x48, Pearson correlation of orig vs port max-channel field: 0.071, -0.042, -0.032, 0.027, 0.002 at t=30.05/30.55/31.05/32.55/34.05 s; binarised (>32) correlation is likewise 0.08 to -0.06. Histogramming the ORIGINAL's hue at the port's bright (>128) pixels gives a flat distribution identical to the histogram at the port's dark pixels — so the port's bright lines do not sit on any particular contour of the original's field.

SENSORS-OFF DIAGNOSTIC (--sensors off, 12 s @ 20 fps) localizes the structural gap as NOT audio-driven: with dead sensors the original still draws smooth continuous rainbow arcs, rings and blobs (mean 35) while the port still draws scattered white/pale speckle (mean 51 — actually BRIGHTER than the original here). So the speckle-vs-blob difference is in the pattern's own geometry/field, and the brightness inversion says the port's audio gain path is what is under-driven, not its base level.

WARM-UP regime (t < ~2 s at 20 fps) is inverted between the sides: the original rails to literally pure white — all 256 px at (255,255,255), saturation 0.00, mean 255 — from t=0.15 to t~1.5 s, then settles to its dense saturated field by ~10 s. The port during that same window is at its densest and most colourful (100% lit, mean 116-134, 11 of 12 hue bins). Consistent with the original's 'Gain' AGC railing on the synthetic feed while the port's does not.

SHARED CORRECT PROPERTIES: both sides are exactly mirror-symmetric about the vertical centre line at every sampled frame (column profiles palindromic on both). Both are resolution-independent — mean brightness barely moves across --grid 8x8 / 16x16 / 48x48 (orig 135/129/134, port 27/30/32 over the same --skip 30 window). Both are seed-independent (seed 1234 vs seed 1: orig 131 vs 129, port 35 vs 30). Both are frame-rate coupled to a similar degree (--skip 20, 6 s: orig 68/164/174 and port 14/28/20 at 10/20/40 fps), so fps coupling is NOT a port-specific finding.

No mode/regime rotation exists: 240 s at 10 fps shows a single homogeneous steady regime on both sides after the warm-up, with per-10 s means flat to within +/-15%. Only two regimes were inspected (warm-up via baseline/dumpA, steady state via late/dense20/grid48).
feedback: Overall brightness/energy is ~6x too low: original holds meanBrightness ~85 (10 fps) / ~130-165 (20 fps) indefinitely, the port holds ~15 / ~30. Whatever the 'Gain' path is, the port is not driving the field anywhere near hard enough on the same beat120 spectrum.

The port must NOT go dark between beats. The original's field is persistent — 80-100% of pixels lit at all times, never dipping below mean ~140 at 20 fps. The port collapses to ~22-30% lit and mean ~5 in the 0.4 s gap between 2 Hz beats, producing a strobe the original does not have. Fix the re-trigger/hold behaviour first (original pixels stay railed at 255 for 10-20 frames before decaying); the fade tail is a secondary issue.

The 'pow fade' decay constant is ~2.3x too aggressive: original multiplies by ~0.80 per frame at 20 fps (half-life 0.155 s), the port by ~0.60 (half-life 0.068 s). Target ~0.80/frame at 20 fps, and note both sides are frame-coupled here so the target is per-frame, not per-second.

Spatial structure is the deepest problem: the port renders single-pixel speckle (neighbour autocorrelation 0.17-0.29) where the original renders contiguous smooth blobs and continuous contour bands (0.44-0.86). Re-render at --grid 48x48 to see it — the original's arcs are solid multi-pixel-wide ribbons, the port's are 1-px broken dotted lines. This is present with --sensors off too, so it is the field/geometry, not the audio response.

Hue span is ~3x too narrow. The original always shows 10-12 of 12 hue bins at once across the grid (a full spatial rainbow, hue varying smoothly with position); the port shows 1-5 bins and at many instants only red + cyan, with a large fraction of pixels rendered pure/near-white (saturation drops to 0.08-0.21 at each beat peak). The hue should be a smooth spatial function of the blot field, not a near-global single tint.

The port's lit pixels do not land where the original's structure is — 48x48 field correlation is |r| < 0.09 at every sampled time, and the original's hue at the port's bright pixels is uniformly distributed. So this is not a palette/exponent remap of a correct field; the blot placement/field itself needs rework, not just the output curve.

Warm-up behaviour is inverted: the original rails to pure white (all 255,255,255) for the first ~1.5-2 s at 20 fps and settles by ~10 s, whereas the port starts at its brightest and most colourful and then falls off. If the original has an auto-gain that ramps up until it saturates on a quiet synthetic feed, the port appears to be missing it or has it pinned low — that single mechanism would explain both the warm-up inversion and the 6x steady-state brightness gap.

Things already right, do not regress them: exact left-right mirror symmetry, resolution independence across 8x8/16x16/48x48, seed independence, sensor binding and 2 Hz beat lock, and the gauge-only control surface (gaugeFeedback / gaugeGain / gaugeComplexity) which matches the original name-for-name and kind-for-kind.
